ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Ernest Hemingway

code.originalText: Six-month review: iron, liver, mood, memory and the plan for maintenance phlebotomy

text.paragraph: Six-month review: iron, liver, mood, memory and blood pressure. [S]

Mr. Hemingway returns six months after intake. He has had twenty-two phlebotomies, and the twenty-third is planned after today's blood tests. He has had no alcohol for about fifteen weeks and still takes naltrexone. His mood is steady; the monthly PHQ-9 with the behavioral health clinician was 6 at his preventive visit and is 5 today. He writes every morning and says names and words come to him more easily. Headaches are about once a week. On amlodipine 10 mg his home average is 124/76, with slight ankle swelling in the evenings. The echocardiogram was done this morning. His guns remain at the club; he would like to bring them home before the autumn shooting season, and this was discussed. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-31; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/78, pulse 72; weight 92.8 kg
Regular rhythm; no murmur; trace ankle edema
Liver not palpable; no spleen felt
Alcohol use disorder, severe; heavy daily drinking for most of his adult life; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented heavy drinking
S — Synthetic modern coding of DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder (seven criteria); person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Raised transferrin saturation and ferritin found on routine intake tests, cause not yet known (heavy drinking, liver disease or iron overload)
S — Synthetic presenting finding; superseded when HFE testing gave the diagnosis.
Hereditary hemochromatosis, HFE C282Y homozygous, with iron overload (ferritin over 1,000 ng/mL) and no advanced liver fibrosis on imaging
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. Whether he had hemochromatosis is disputed (CLM-0013); the modern diagnosis is not offered as proof of it.
Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate; Mood Disorder Questionnaire negative and no history of mania or hypomania
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; not a claim about his real mood. The roster's bipolar disorder lead is disputed (CLM-0014) and is not used.
Essential hypertension, stage 2, with heavy drinking contributing
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed by home readings.

Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, slowed thinking and forgetfulness) after repeated head injuries, most recently a concussion with a skull fracture a year ago; chronic traumatic encephalopathy is not diagnosed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented head injuries; alcohol and depression also affect the symptoms.
S — Synthetic finding on diabetes screening; iron overload and alcohol both raise the risk of diabetes.
Fishhook puncture wound of the right hand with early cellulitis after saltwater exposure, in a man with iron overload; treated with antibiotics covering Vibrio; resolved
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

value.displayName: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate

list.item:
Hereditary hemochromatosis on weekly phlebotomy (E83.110). Ferritin 268 ng/mL and transferrin saturation 44% after twenty-two sessions; hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL. Echocardiogram shows no iron-related cardiomyopathy. About two more months of weekly sessions should reach a ferritin of 50 to 100 ng/mL. [S]
Continue weekly phlebotomy; ferritin every four sessions as the target nears.
Then maintenance phlebotomy about every two to four months to keep ferritin 50 to 100 ng/mL.
Liver stiffness to be rechecked after iron removal.

Alcohol use disorder, severe, in early remission (F10.20). About fifteen weeks without alcohol; liver tests and MCV are normal. [S]
Continue naltrexone 50 mg daily for at least another six months.
Stop thiamine.

Depression on sertraline (F32.1). PHQ-9 5 from 16: a response, close to remission. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or wishes to be dead. He asked to bring his guns home for the shooting season; after discussion he chose to keep them at the club until he has been well for a few more months, and to store them locked and unloaded with the ammunition separate when they come home. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline remains in his phone. [S]
Continue sertraline 100 mg for at least six to twelve months after remission.
Psychotherapy every two weeks.
Firearm storage reviewed again at the next visit.

Hypertension (I10). At target on amlodipine 10 mg; trace ankle edema, which he does not mind. Echocardiogram shows mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal function. [S]
Continue amlodipine 10 mg daily.
Kidney function, potassium and urine albumin at the yearly review.

Post-concussion symptoms (F07.81). MoCA 27 from 25, with better delayed recall, and fewer headaches after months without alcohol. Neuropsychological testing is not needed now. [S]
Continue the headache and sleep plan; repeat MoCA in a year or sooner for any decline.

Prediabetes (R73.03). HbA1c 5.9% from 6.1%. Lipids improved without alcohol; estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk about 6%, so a statin is not recommended now. [S]
HbA1c and lipids yearly.

Ferritin 50 to 100 ng/mL with weekly phlebotomy, then maintenance. Outcome by 2026-08-31: Ferritin 1,460 to 268 ng/mL after twenty-two sessions; induction continuing [S]
PHQ-9 below 5. Outcome by 2026-08-31: PHQ-9 16 to 5 at six months; response, nearly in remission [S]
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg. Outcome by 2026-08-31: 126/78 in clinic and an average of 124/76 at home on amlodipine 10 mg [S]
Fewer headaches and clearer thinking, so that he can write. Outcome by 2026-08-31: Headaches once a week from three; MoCA 25 to 27; writing every morning [S]

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis: 2011 practice guideline by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2011); ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (2019); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Major Depressive Disorder (2022); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management and Rehabilitation of Post-Acute Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (2021); Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)
Follow-up: Weekly phlebotomy until ferritin is 50 to 100 ng/mL, then maintenance. Review in three months. Psychotherapy every two weeks and monthly PHQ-9. Colonoscopy as scheduled. [S]
